item.title: Steelers coach Mike McCarthy drops cryptic upate on DeShon Elliott injury
item.description: Barry Reeger-Imagn Images Steelers coach Mike McCarthy drops cryptic upate on DeShon Elliott injury appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Pittsburgh Steelers suffered a lopsided loss to the Cincinnati Bengals on Sunday Night Football , and head coach Mike McCarthy did not offer many answers on DeShon Elliott’s surprise absence afterward. Elliott was a late scratch for the 38-18 defeat in Cincinnati after injuring his knee during pregame warmups . When asked about the safety’s status after the game, McCarthy kept his update vague. “During his warm-up, he had something that showed up,” McCarthy said in a post-game press conference, via Chris Adamski of TribLive. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Mike McCarthy on DeShon Elliott being a late scratch for what the team announced as a knee injury: “During his warmup he had something that showed up.” — Chris Adamski (@C_AdamskiTrib) November 16, 2026 It was a frustrating development for Elliott, who has been healthy for only two games this season and was expected to return to the lineup coming out of Pittsburgh’s bye week. Instead, he was ruled inactive shortly before kickoff. Pittsburgh was also without cornerback Sean Murphy-Bunting, who was among the team’s inactives. The knee issue also brings back bad memories for the veteran defensive back. Last season, Elliott suffered a knee injury in a Sunday night loss to the Green Bay Packers that was expected to sideline him for the rest of the year, just months after he signed a two-year contract extension with the Steelers. Without Elliott, Pittsburgh’s secondary had no answers for Joe Burrow. The Bengals quarterback completed 35-of-44 passes for 409 yards and four touchdowns, two of which went to Chase Brown. Burrow threw three of those scores in the second quarter alone, sending Cincinnati into halftime with a 24-3 lead . The Bengals piled up 484 total yards and built a 31-3 lead before the Steelers found the end zone. Aaron Rodgers threw two late touchdown passes , one to DK Metcalf and the other to Pat Freiermuth, but the comeback attempt came far too late. Pittsburgh managed just 222 total yards. The loss snapped Pittsburgh’s four-game winning streak and dropped the Steelers to 6-3 on the season. McCarthy and the Steelers will now await more clarity on Elliott’s knee as they prepare to visit the Philadelphia Eagles next Sunday. item.title: Evening at the improv? Brock Purdy, Christian McCaffrey make sure 49ers, fans enjoyed show
item.description: San Francisco 49ers running back Christian McCaffrey breaks away from the Dallas Cowboys defense for a 74-yard touchdown in the second quarter Sunday in Arlington, Texas. Tight end George Kittle (85) kept him clear of defenders. (Tom Fox/The Dallas Morning News) ARLINGTON, Texas - The offensive explosion began with improvisation. On Sunday, with the San Francisco 49ers trailing by six points and facing 3rd-and-8 at their 26-yard line, one play away from punting for the second time in their first four possessions, head coach Kyle Shanahan called a play in which wide receiver Keenan Allen was quarterback Brock Purdy 's first read. But Allen, running an in-breaking route nine yards downfield, was blanketed by cornerback Joey Porter. Purdy looked to his left to his second read, wideout Deebo Samuel . Nope. Covered. Meanwhile, Purdy's pocket was crumbling. Linebacker Shemar James blitzed. So did safety Caleb Downs. Purdy's internal clock went off. "I felt like I sort of had to get going," Purdy said. What happened next opened the floodgates in the 49ers' 46-40 win in which they gained 584 yards, the fifth-most in franchise history, and became the first team with three offensive touchdowns of 65-plus yards since 2000. As Purdy raced to his right, prepared to try to scramble for a first down, running back Christian McCaffrey made it a two-man improv act. McCaffrey's assignment on a play in which tight end George Kittle and wide receiver Jordan Watkins also ran routes didn't foreshadow glory. "He was in protection (blocking)," Shanahan said. Things changed. After McCaffrey leaned his right shoulder into defensive tackle Kenny Clark, he stopped for a split second, surrounded by three offensive linemen, before realizing Purdy was keeping the play alive. Scramble-drill mode. "It's just some backyard football," McCaffrey said. McCaffrey, in the middle of the field, near the line of scrimmage, initially broke to his right, into the flat, but he was running with James, who was chasing Purdy toward the sideline. McCaffrey instinctively cut upfield to daylight, splitting two defenders, just as Purdy had decided to try to run for the first down. "There's a point where it's like, ‘All right, I think I can try to use my legs now at this moment,'" Purdy said. "And I was going to do that." Things changed. At full speed, Purdy, seeing McCaffrey all alone around the 35-yard line, violently slammed on the brakes, just a yard away from crossing the line of scrimmage. "It's those little decisions that you make in games," McCaffrey said. "For Brock to not scramble - to not just surrender the play - but to keep it alive. That's a big deal." But as we saw on Sunday, New Orleans has also come up short on multiple occasions. New Orleans was tied with the Carolina Panthers late in the fourth quarter on Sunday. Carolina had possession of the football, but needed a good chunk of yards to get in field goal range. A penalty on Kool-Aid McKinstry ensured the Panthers got those yards. Even with the McKinstry penalty on the final drive, the defense played well. Linebacker Kaden Elliss showed out, recording 15 tackles, a sack, and two tackles for a loss. The Saints will need to figure things out sooner rather than later. This loss sets them back in the NFC South race. But they remain alive nonetheless. item.title: Thunder center Aday Mara’s double-double night draws Mark Daigneault eye-opening take
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Scott Marshall-Imagn Images Thunder center Aday Mara’s double-double night draws Mark Daigneault eye-opening take appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Oklahoma City Thunder got back in the win column against the Sacramento Kings on Sunday, and rookie Aday Mara earned some high praise from head coach Mark Daigneault for his role in it. Mara posted a double-double with 16 points and 13 rebounds in 25 minutes off the bench as the Thunder cruised to a 125-103 win at Golden 1 Center. The 7-foot-3 big man shot an efficient 8-of-11 from the field and added three assists. After the game, Daigneault liked what he saw from the youngster , but he also made it clear that Mara cannot rest on one good night. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “He got into the game and played better as he went. It’s a good experience for him, understanding you’ve got to get yourself back to the bottom of the mountain every night, and you’ve got to start climbing,” Daigneault said after the game, via Nick Gallo of the Thunder. Mara did much of his damage on the offensive glass, hauling in eight offensive rebounds that led to 12 second-chance points. The rookie has been getting more opportunities lately with Chet Holmgren sidelined by a knee injury. Mara has been splitting time with Isaiah Hartenstein in the frontcourt and also posted a 10-point, 10-rebound double-double against the Portland Trail Blazers last week. Of course, Shai Gilgeous-Alexander was the star of the show for Oklahoma City . The superstar guard poured in 37 points on 13-of-20 shooting, including 4-of-5 from deep, in just 29 minutes. Ajay Mitchell, who returned from a two-game absence due to an ankle sprain , chipped in 14 points and five assists. Alex Caruso added 11 points and four steals, while Hartenstein grabbed 11 rebounds. The victory snapped a three-game losing streak for the Thunder, who improved to 9-5 and wrapped up a four-game road trip, their longest of the season. Sacramento, meanwhile, dropped to 1-12 and has now lost six straight games. Oklahoma City will return home to host the Atlanta Hawks on Wednesday. item.title: Morgan Rogers starts as England beat the World Champions
item.description: MADRID, SPAIN - NOVEMBER 15: Morgan Rogers of England competes for the ball with Marc Cucurella of Spain during the UEFA Nations League 2026/27 group phase match between Spain and England at Wanda Metropolitano on November 15, 2026 in Madrid, Spain. (Photo by Manuel Queimadelos/Quality Sport Images/Getty Images) | Getty Images Morgan Rogers started while both sides fielded ex-Chelsea left backs in last night’s Nations League encounter at the Metropolitano in Madrid. Neither of those is likely to be the most memorable story from England’s impressive 3-2 win over the World Champions, but that’s what shook out from the Chelsea filter. It was in fact a direct matchup between Rogers and Marc Cucurella on England’s right, while on the left flank, former Academy standout Lewis Hall was having a good old time running forward with the ball. That was a bit of a theme for the Three Lions, having a good old time — at least until Elliot Anderson’s red card. Then it was shades of Mexico City, hanging on for the massive win. Thankfully, Jordan Henderson did not break his arm jumping over the advertising hoardings in celebration this time (probably because he wasn’t there). England, who came out with tremendous energy, built a scarcely believable three-nil lead at one point against the defending European and World Champions, with Harry Kane winning and scoring a penalty late in the first half, followed by a quickfire double from Ezri Konsa and Ben White as the game approached its hour mark. But then, Anderson made a very bad decision, giving away a penalty with a needless shirt-pull and getting sent off as well for not even attempting to play the ball, and from then on, it was hang-on time. Mikel Oyarzabal converted and Nico Williams scored just a few minutes after arriving on the scene to set up a grandstand finish. But we know how an inspired Tuchel team can rise to the occasion — even Rogers was defending! — and this was certainly a fine example of that. With the win, England are in the Nations League quarterfinals. Morgan Rogers played the full 90; he had no further comments about the Cole Palmer situation. Elsewhere, Roméo Lavia was back after sitting out Belgium’s last game due to suspension, and played 76 minutes in their 4-1 win over Marco Palestra’s Italy, 4-1. Mike Penders was an unused substitute as Belgium have now also qualified for the quarterfinals — finishing runners-up in their group to France, who beat Turkey, 2-1. Malo Gusto, after a performance that drew some rather terrible reviews last time out, was an unused substitute.

item.title: Rams’ Aaron Donald opens up on health status after win vs. Cardinals
item.description: David Brytus-Imagn Images Rams’ Aaron Donald opens up on health status after win vs. Cardinals appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Aaron Donald gave the Los Angeles Rams another reason to feel good after their 42-10 win over the Arizona Cardinals. The veteran defensive tackle recorded 1.5 sacks that ended a lengthy drought and cleared out any doubts regarding his physical condition heading into the team’s bye week. Donald described his true emotions after the victory, particularly because the Rams’ defense spent relatively little time on the field. However, he still wants to use the break to get fully healthy before the team’s final stretch. “Get back right, get myself feeling 100% and get ready for this run,” Donald said. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The performance against Arizona marked Donald’s first sack in 1,050 days. That stretch included two seasons in retirement before he returned to the Rams in late August. His previous sack came on New Year’s Eve in 2023 against the New York Giants. Donald finished Sunday’s game with an eight-game streak without one. He also moved past Justin Houston and Chandler Jones, who each finished their careers with 112 sacks, into 31st place on the NFL’s all-time list. The Rams’ defense delivered an impressive performance apart from just Donald’s individual numbers. Los Angeles held Arizona to 123 total yards and six first downs, both the lowest totals by any team this season. The Cardinals also failed to convert any of their six third-down attempts. Additionally, head coach Sean McVay praised Donald’s continued impact on the team. “I’m never surprised,” McVay said. “He never ceases to amaze me. I think the term ‘1 of 1’ is thrown around way too loosely this day and age, but it’s not with him. He’s 1 of 1.” The Rams have won four straight games after opening the season 2-4. They will use their Week 11 bye to recover before returning to action against the Green Bay Packers. item.title: ‘One-horse race’ – Bengals QB Joe Burrow’s historic performance against Steelers leads to MVP calls
item.description: Photo by Jeff Moreland/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Cincinnati Bengals QB Joe Burrow made history in their 38-18 win over the Pittsburgh Steelers in an MVP-worthy performance. Burrow matched Peyton Manning’s long-standing record for most consecutive games (five) with four or more touchdowns with his four-TD performance against the Pittsburgh Steelers. The 29-year-old QB is emerging as the frontrunner for the MVP award this season, and this performance against the Steelers seems to have convinced everyone it’s finally Burrow’s year. Joe Burrow hailed as MVP after incredible win over Steelers Burrow ended the game going 35/44 on pass attempts for 409 yards, four touchdowns, zero interceptions and a 135.7 passer rating. Fans think the MVP race has already been shut by Burrow amid his incredible season. “Joe Burrow has full game stats at halftime. Yeah, this is a one-horse race for the MVP,” were the thoughts of one fan . “Hard to argue against Joe Burrow being the MVP favourite right now. Now it’s time for him to actually live up to his clutch reputation in the playoffs. No excuses. 2 elite WR’s, great offensive line. Get it done,” said a fan . “Again, Joe Burrow is the MVP rn. Idga- who my team is; that’s just an objective football fact at this point,” said another fan deeming Burrow as the MVP . “Yeah man, give Burrow the MVP,” said another fan . “Joe Burrow has 302 yards and 3 touchdowns… In the FIRST HALF. Just give him the MVP,” said one more fan vouching for Burrow’s MVP case . Burrow has a 74.7 completion percentage (254/340) this season for 2,795 yards, 27 touchdowns, and six interceptions with a 117.7 passer rating. He leads the NFL in passing touchdowns and is among the leaders in completion percentage, passer rating, EPA, and other metrics, also ranking No. 1 on PFF for QBs this season. Burrow is currently considered the favourite for the MVP award ahead of other QBs such as Josh Allen and Brock Purdy. If Burrow can continue this winning pace and production, it’s hard to see anyone beating him out for the award this season. Trevor Lawrence has remained the barometer for the Jacksonville Jaguars , leading the team to its third straight win after disposing of the Tennessee Titans , 40-23, at Nissan Stadium on Sunday. Lawrence went 25-of-35 for 352 yards and three touchdowns. He also had four carries for 27 yards. The Jaguars notched their sixth win in seven games and improved to 7-2 to extend their lead in the AFC South. The Titans, meanwhile, fell to 1-8, including 0-5 at home. Just having the confidence. I know what I’m seeing. I’ve seen these plays a lot. I’ve seen the coverages. I feel like I’m processing really well right now, and that’s a huge part of it. But then it all comes back to our guys, our players, the guys making plays. item.title: Luka Doncic Sends A Message To Lakers After Suns’ Fourth-Quarter Rally
item.description: Los Angeles Lakers v Phoenix Suns Getty Luka Doncic had 37 points through three quarters and figured his work was done for the afternoon. Instead, he had to check back in to help the Los Angeles Lakers finish off the Phoenix Suns. The Lakers won 131-123 on Sunday for their eighth straight victory, but Doncic used his postgame interview to tell his team what it needs to do better. “I wasn’t planning on playing in the fourth quarter; we need to get better at that. I know we played badly, we finished badly, but we need to improve in that area. When we manage to get ahead, we have to hold on to the lead, and we have to work on that.” Phoenix scored 43 points in the fourth quarter, matching Doncic’s total for the entire game. A lead that reached 31 in the third was down to five with just over a minute to play. By then, Doncic was back on the floor, and the Lakers still needed one more big shot. View this post on Instagram Luka Doncic returns as the Lakers’ lead shrinks The Lakers were up 101-70 with 1:47 to go in the third. They still had a 24-point cushion when the fourth began. Phoenix kept chipping away, and Lakers coach JJ Redick took a timeout with roughly five minutes left and the margin down to single digits. The Suns won the quarter 43-27. Doncic pointed to Phoenix’s increased aggression and said the Lakers got sloppy coming out for the fourth. He also took hold of the coaching whiteboard to address teammates during the game, according to Bleacher Report. Quentin Grimes gave Los Angeles breathing room in the final minute. With the Lakers ahead 126-121, he banked in a three to push the margin back to eight. Doncic added two free throws to close out the win. Grimes finished with 22 points, and Doncic paired his 43 with nine assists, per the box score. Lakers lean on Doncic with Austin Reaves out The Lakers played without Austin Reaves , who bruised his left heel in Milwaukee last week. Reaves entered Sunday averaging 24.7 points and 4.7 assists, leaving Los Angeles without one of its primary scorers and playmakers. Doncic put up 20 points in the first quarter alone. He made three shots from beyond the arc and went 7-for-8 from the line in those opening 12 minutes. Late in the third, he drew MVP chants in Phoenix after converting a three-point play. Phoenix was the last stop on a trip that took the Lakers through Detroit, Atlanta, and Milwaukee. Los Angeles had three days off after the Milwaukee game and finished the trip with a 12-2 record. Redick had credited the team’s offensive organization and disruptive defense during the winning streak while pointing to ball security and defensive rotations as areas that still needed work , as reported by the Los Angeles Times. He also said Reaves was improving and that his availability would come down to how much pain he could tolerate. Los Angeles returns home Tuesday to face the Charlotte Hornets at Crypto.com Arena. item.description: 1 penalty saved, 3 stops, 100% run-outs: Man United keeper Senne Lammens regains form on international stage Manchester United had two players in international action on Sunday evening in a busy night of Nations League action. Senne Lammens The Belgian Manchester United goalkeeper Senne Lammens has not had the best of seasons for Manchester United this year. Nonetheless, he has had a consistent run in the national team owing to Thibaut Courtois taking a break from international football after the World Cup. Lammens has been quite impressive in the group as his side finished second, one point behind France. According to SofaScore, he made three saves in their impressive 4-1 win over Italy, including a penalty stop in additional time at the end of the match. It was a strong right-handed stop after guessing the right way, which will do his confidence the world of good. Lammens also completed his only run-out, made a high claim and one punch to protect his goal. The only blemish was his passing, as he completed just 59% of his passes and only 25% of his long-ball attempts. Lammens also made a clearance and will hope to take this form into United’s huge game against Liverpool on Sunday. Unusually, he didn’t make any tackles or compete in any duels in the centre of the pitch, but he did make two clearances and blocked one shot defensively. Maybe it’s the relief of finally winning a game, coupled with the fact we’d played nine matches inside a month. It’s been a grueller, and we’ve been tremendously busy because of the sheer frequency of the fixtures. Whatever the reason, I think I’ve needed to switch off from it all (wey, to some extent). Quite a few people noted that I wasn’t my usual hyper self after we beat Chelsea. item.title: LeBron James says he’s just done something he never thought he would do in his career
item.description: Photo by Andy Lyons/Getty Images LeBron James continues to make history in his 24th season in the NBA. The 41-year-old started for the Philadelphia 76ers in their 131-124 win against the Indiana Pacers on Sunday, and The King was in great form. James recorded 11 assists against the Pacers, and that took him past an iconic name in the all-time NBA assists charts. He says he never saw that coming. LeBron James says he didn’t foresee ranking third on the NBA career assists list James is one of the most complete players the NBA has ever seen. Over the course of his 24-year-long career, the four-time champion has played in all five positions on the court, and he has amassed incredible numbers under every metric. On Sunday, James took his career assists tally to 12,092, surpassing Hall of Fame point guard Jason Kidd to rank third on the list. That is an incredible achievement, one James says he is humbled by, but he has revealed that he never foresaw achieving this in his career. He said: “It’s super humbling. It’s something that I didn’t obviously foresee in my career. But I knew assists meant a lot to me. Just the movement of the ball, being able to find my teammates and put the ball on time and on target. “And also just being linked with some of the greats to have ever played this game, and also a dear friend of mine, J Kidd, is really special.” James now ranks third on the all-time assists list, below leader John Stockton, who recorded 15,806 career assists, and Chris Paul, who assisted 12,552 times. Ironically, James was on the Redeem Team of 2008 along with Kidd and Paul. He has overtaken one, and it now remains to be seen if he can do the same to the other before the end of this season. Getty The Detroit Lions have a gigantic void to fill on defense after edge rusher Aidan Hutchinson suffered a season-ending injury, but could add a former Super Bowl champion as a bargain replacement. Hutchinson was hurt early in Sunday’s win over the New England Patriots, falling to the turf after leaping in the air while celebrating a sack of quarterback Drake Maye. Hutchinson was ruled out and is feared to have suffered a torn ACL, which would put him out for the season. Lions Could Grab Former Super Bowl Champion to Fill Defensive Void The Lions had already suffered another blow when linebacker Jack Campbell suffered a serious injury, and now may need to hit free agency to account for Hutchinson’s loss. While the Lions have yet to make an official statement on Hutchinson’s future, the injury is feared to keep him out for the remainder of the season. There are some internal options the team could consider, but there is also at least one veteran who could join the team in free agency. Bleacher Report’s Moe Moton identified 10-year veteran Leonard Floyd as a potential “bargain” addition for a team in need of pass rush help. “Beset by injuries early in his career, Leonard Floyd didn’t miss a game between 2018 and 2024,” Moton wrote. “Though Floyd bounced around the league in his prime, he was highly productive after his four-year stint with the Chicago Bears.” Moton noted that Floyd has some very productive seasons in his recent history, along with a Super Bowl season with the Los Angeles Rams. “Floyd registered at least 8.5 sacks in five consecutive seasons between 2020 and 2024, helping the Los Angeles Rams win Super Bowl LVI over the Cincinnati Bengals with five tackles and a sack,” Moton wrote. Moton suggested that Floyd could still have at least a bit of the athleticism that helped him accumulate 70 career sacks. “At 34, Floyd may have lost a step that allows him to close on quarterbacks, but he can still move a signal-caller off his spot with pressure off the edge,” Moton wrote. “The 10-year pro is best suited as a stopgap defender.” Lions Waiting for Official News on Aidan Hutchinson Lions head coach Dan Campbell said after Sunday’s 35-10 win that the team would need to return to the United States from Germany before they could make a final assessment. item.title: ‘Might Be the Greatest Offensive Player Ever,’ ‘The MVP Season We’ve All Been Waiting For’ — NBA World Marvels As Luka Dončić’s Historic Start Continues
item.description: 'Might Be the Greatest Offensive Player Ever,' 'The MVP Season We've All Been Waiting For' — NBA World Marvels As Luka Dončić's Historic Start Continues Luka Dončić poured in a game-high 43 points Sunday as the shorthanded Los Angeles Lakers held off the Phoenix Suns 131-123 on the road for their eighth straight win. That marked the superstar guard’s seventh 40-point game in just 12 appearances this season. The eye-popping pace left the NBA world digging through the record books and further amplified the two-time scoring champion’s early MVP buzz. Luka Dončić’s Wilt Chamberlain-Esque Start Earns High Praise Dončić rolled his ankle in Wednesday’s 123-112 road win over the Milwaukee Bucks but didn’t miss a game or skip a beat. (Photo by Vaughn Ridley/Getty Images) Getty Edmonton Oilers superstar Connor McDavid has been chasing down Wayne Gretzky throughout his entire career, but now he’s tied one of his records once again. Heading into Sunday’s game, Gretzky was the sole player in NHL history to record 40 assists in just 22 games. Even then, he was only able to do so once in his career. He did it in 23 games on two occasions, but he was never able to do it in 22 games again following the 1984-85 season. Then, as the Edmonton Oilers faced the Philadelphia Flyers on Sunday night, McDavid became the second to do so, as first reported by Sportsnet. When Leon Draisaitl scored his 19th goal of the season just 8:08 into the first period, McDavid picked up the primary assist on the play, his 40th of the season in the Oilers’ 22nd game. He then picked up his 41st assist of the season later in the period with another primary helper, this time scored by Zach Hyman. He’s currently pacing to become just the second player in league history to surpass 200 points in a single season. The only player to do so is the aforementioned Gretzky, who did so four times. Mendoza had been waiting for his opportunity to start after weeks of calls from Raiders fans for him to replace Kirk Cousins. However, his first outing also showed how much work lies ahead. Mendoza’s afternoon was made more difficult by the loss of star tight end Brock Bowers to an injury early in the contest. His availability could become an important factor as Las Vegas looks for more production from its passing game. The numbers also showed the difference between the two offences. Seattle finished with 382 total yards compared with just 163 for the Raiders, while Drew Lock completed 14 of 17 passes for 240 yards and two touchdowns. item.title: Cowboys’ Jerry Jones Makes Statement on George Pickens Future Despite ‘Disappointment’
item.description: George Pickens #3 of the Dallas Cowboys Getty The Dallas Cowboys‘ loss to the 49ers on Sunday featured so many distressing defensive play that it would be easy to overlook the fact that quarterback Dak Prescott poured just about all he had into the game, repeatedly pulling the team back from what appeared to be desperate deficits to give Dallas a chance late in the game. And it would be easy to overlook the fact that, without question, receiver George Pickens had his best game of the season, the kind of game many had been waiting for here in his second go-round with the Cowboys. Not only did Pickens catch 11 passes (he did have at least two drops, however) but he tallied 145 yards and three touchdowns, repeatedly going at and beating the 49ers’ Demmodore Lenoir. The Cowboys lost, 46-40, and fell to 4-6 on the season in doing so. But the breakout game for Pickens will at least re-ignite the question of just how good this offense can be when it is clicking–and when both Lamb and Pickens (who had a hamstring injury and missed Week 9) are healthy and working the field. Jerry Jones Sees ‘Positive’ of George Pickens After the game, as so often happens, Cowboys owner Jerry Jones held court with reporters and was asked about the way Pickens played–and whether seeing the offense look so productive affects how Jones might consider paying Pickens in free agency next winter. Said Jones when asked if he thinks the Cowboys can build around Pickens: “I sure do. George is a positive, a real positive. They do some outstanding things with George and Dak, CeeDee. Those should be big assets for us and tonight, I have to say they kept us where we at least thought if some good things happened at the end, we might have a chance. item.title: 'It's not the end of the world' - Aymeric Laporte urges Spain to be 'self-critical' after failing to take enough risks on the ball in 3-2 loss to England
item.description: Spain v England - UEFA Nations League 2026/27 Group A3 MD6 - Getty Images Sport Spain centre-back Aymeric Laporte has called on his team-mates to examine their own shortcomings after suffering a 3-2 UEFA Nations League defeat against England in Madrid on Sunday. The loss at the Metropolitano ended the reigning European and world champions' 43-game unbeaten streak in regulation play stretching back to March 2024. Defender calls for honest reflection Laporte felt the hosts were too cautious in possession as their remarkable run without a regulation-time defeat - setting aside a penalty shootout loss to Portugal in the 2025 Nations League final - finally came to an end . Having learned from the cautious approach that cost them in this summer's World Cup semi-final defeat against Argentina in Atlanta, Thomas Tuchel's visitors attacked relentlessly from the opening whistle. Inspired by Jude Bellingham, the Three Lions overwhelmed a passive Spanish side for an hour . Centre-back laments cautious ball progression After wasting several early openings, England took the lead on the stroke of half-time when captain Harry Kane netted his 93rd international goal from the penalty spot following a foul by Pau Cubarsi. Ezri Konsa then headed in Declan Rice's 53rd-minute corner before Arsenal defender Ben White capped a sweeping move with a powerful angled finish four minutes later to make it 3-0. Speaking to UEFA after the final whistle, Laporte reflected on his side's uncharacteristically timid display: "This is a moment where we have to be a little analytical and a little self-critical. After all these games unbeaten, it's a case of starting over. I'd rather look at ourselves than talk about England because, during our long run, we've played an approach which is taking more risks with the ball. It has worked for us, but I don't think we did enough of that tonight. It's not the end of the world in a footballing sense. We've qualified, and we simply have to start over." Late red card sparks rally England handed their hosts a lifeline in the 65th minute when Jarell Quansah was caught in possession and Elliot Anderson was shown a straight red card for pulling back Lamine Yamal, allowing Mikel Oyarzabal to convert the resulting spot-kick. Suddenly inspired with Yamal acting as the catalyst, Spain cut the deficit further in the 75th minute when the winger delivered a cross for substitute Nico Williams to fire in off the left post. Trafford heroics decide group winners Despite facing a frantic late siege from the hosts, England goalkeeper James Trafford justified his selection by producing a string of outstanding saves and blocks across the final 15 minutes to preserve the 3-2 win. While Tuchel's side advance to March's Nations League quarter-finals as group winners following the finest display of the German's tenure, Spain progress as runners-up. Consequently, La Roja will look to rebuild their momentum when the two-legged knockout ties get underway next spring.

item.title: Lobos Look to Bounce Back From UNLV Loss With Mountain West Title Still in Reach
item.description: ALBUQUERQUE, N.M. (KRQE) – The New Mexico Lobos are turning the page after a difficult loss to UNLV, but their goals for the season remain firmly in sight. The Rebels became the first opponent in more than a year to score more than 20 points against the Lobos, handing New Mexico a setback after a strong season. Now, head coach Jason Eck is challenging his team to stick together, learn from the loss and respond. Lobos look to improve after UNLV setback New Mexico struggled to stretch the field vertically against UNLV, limiting its opportunities to create explosive plays through the air. One highlight came from a trick play, as freshman Bailen George connected with fellow freshman DJ Darling for a 65-yard gain — the Lobos' longest pass play of the game. Despite the flashes of offensive potential, UNLV found ways to take advantage of New Mexico's struggles and pull away in the second half. Eck emphasized the importance of accountability as the team looks to move forward. “We got to improve in all facets, and again, I think we got to stick together. We can't be pointing fingers at others,” Eck said. “Everybody has to look at what we can do better to improve on this journey. We got to see how we respond to adversity.” Championship goals remain in sight Despite the loss, the Lobos believe there's still plenty to play for this season. Eck pointed to the team's remaining opportunities, including a chance to compete for a Mountain West championship and reach double-digit wins. “We still can control a conference championship. We can control double-digit wins. So, I mean, those were really our true goals,” Eck said. Offensive lineman Malik Aliane also encouraged the team's younger players to embrace their opportunities and continue developing. Defensive end Darren Agu echoed that confidence, emphasizing that New Mexico still has a chance to compete for the conference title. “We bounce back. Obviously, we still got the Mountain West to play for,” Agu said. What's next for the Lobos? New Mexico won't have much time to dwell on the loss, with a quick turnaround ahead. The Lobos hit the road Friday to face Wyoming in another important Mountain West matchup.
